message:
Security: improve JSON path validation

## Summary
This change hardens JSON path handling in the abstract query generator by tightening how path expressions are constructed before being appended to the generated SQL.

## Motivation
JSON path fragments can originate from dynamic model/query composition, so we should avoid stitching path syntax together inline where possible. Building the path operand through the existing escaping pathway improves validation at the query-construction boundary and reduces the chance of malformed path content being interpreted unexpectedly.

## What changed
- Route the assembled `'{...}'` JSON path through `self.escape(...)`
- Use the escaped value when constructing the `#>>` expression instead of concatenating the raw path literal directly

## Security impact
This is a defensive hardening change:
- strengthens input handling for dynamically assembled JSON paths
- centralizes quoting/escaping through the existing generator boundary
- reduces exposure to malformed path payloads and parser edge cases
- improves overall security posture without changing intended query semantics

## Notes
The behavior of valid queries should remain the same; the main effect is stricter, safer construction of the JSON path operand in generated SQL.
